title: Temporal segmented canary controller with rollback heuristics
author: Sana Patel
description:
Motivation: We need finer-grained control for canary releases that respects temporal user segments (timezone/active-window), session affinity, and short-lived metric shocks. Current staged canaries at Redwood focus on percentage-based splits and cohort anchors; customers asked for time-windowed phasing (e.g., release to early-morning users first) and a conservative rollback fence for rapid metric regressions during local peak windows. This PR introduces a Temporal Segmented Canary Controller (TSCC) with heuristic rollback scoring and session-affinity reconciliation.

What this PR does: Adds a controller that can schedule canary percentage ramps bound to temporal segment definitions (time-of-day, local timezone, business hours), maintain session-affine buckets to avoid mid-session model swaps, and run an automated rollback heuristic that combines rate-of-change of key SLOs, cohort drift scores, and cross-segment divergence. The rollback heuristic uses a decaying severity score so transient blips are deprioritized while sustained degradations trigger an automated rollback.

Key behaviors: 1) Temporal fencing: define segments by cron-like windows and user timezone mapping so traffic can be phased across local-active windows. 2) Segment-aware shadowing: sample-preserving shadow runs that maintain the same user-session routing to avoid introduction bias when promoting. 3) Session-affinity reconciliation: a small sticky-lease to avoid replacing a model mid-session (configurable TTL). 4) Rollback heuristic: weighted aggregation of latency P95 delta, error-rate delta, quality-regression signal (from eval hooks), and session-conflict rate. 5) Visibility: emits per-segment metrics, a confidence score time-series, and a suggested action label for the Console rollout timeline.

Compatibility: Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRD. New optional fields are added to the rollout spec (temporalSegments, sessionAffinityTTL, rollbackWeights, confidenceDecaySeconds). If omitted, controller defaults to legacy percentage ramps.

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover scheduler edge windows (DST boundaries), session-affinity transitions, and heuristic math. Integration test harness runs simulated traffic across 6 timezones and validates that rollouts respect windows and that automated rollback triggers only on sustained metric regressions. End-to-end smoke includes Canaries + Shadow promotion flow against the mock serving runtime.

Release plan: Merge to main behind feature flag rollout.temporal_canaries. Rollout on infra staging for 2 weeks then enable for early access customers. Observability dashboard panel and alert rules are included to monitor per-segment confidence and session-conflict counters.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: ENG-2145 linked
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Console dashboard wiring
- [x] Backwards compatibility with rollout CRD
- [x] Feature flag gating

Notes: This is targeted at customers running production canaries where traffic locality and business-hour exposures matter (e.g., financial trading hours, regionally-peaked consumer services). The rollback heuristic parameters will be tuned in staging before general availability.
commit_summary: controller: add temporal segment scheduler and API bindings
runtime-client: preserve session affinity during shadow runs
safety: implement rollback scoring and decay policy
console: add per-segment timeline annotations and suggested action labels
tests: add integration scenarios for timezone phasing and session TTLs
docs: rollout CRD examples and upgrade notes
review_thread: Miguel Torres: Nice work on the scheduling API. Two comments: can we make the sessionAffinityTTL configurable per-segment? In some mobile-heavy segments we want shorter TTLs.
Sana Patel: Good point — made sessionAffinityTTL segment-scoped and added validation to ensure TTL <= 24h. See service/rollout/session_affinity.go + unit tests.
Aisha Khan: The rollbackWeights default favors latency over quality. We should document the rationale and provide a safe default for customers who opt-in without tuning.
Sana Patel: Added default weights (latency:0.4, error_rate:0.3, quality:0.2, session_conflict:0.1) and a comment block in docs/operations/rollout_temporal_segments.md explaining tradeoffs.

Daniel Li: Integration test failure on DST boundary scenario — reproduction in tests/integration/temporal_canary_test.go line 128. I see you handle timezone offsets but not repeated wall-clock hour during fallback.
Sana Patel: Fixed DST handling by normalizing to local date boundaries using tzdb-aware library and added additional unit test to cover the repeated hour. Re-ran integration tests.
Aisha Khan: Approving once we add a short note to the Console UI that temporal segments are feature-flagged and may be disabled in older clusters.
Sana Patel: Added console UI note and a feature flag check before rendering timeline segment controls. CI green, merging.
merge_commit_message:
Squash: Temporal segmented canary controller + rollback heuristics

Adds TSCC with temporal segments, session affinity, and automated rollback scoring. Includes console wiring and tests.
release_notes: Experimental: Temporal segmented canaries (feature flag rollout.temporal_canaries). Allows scheduling canary ramps by local time windows, preserves session affinity during shadowing, and enables automated rollback heuristics that aggregate latency, error-rate, and quality signals. Backwards compatible with existing rollout CRD when fields omitted.
notes_for_oncall: If an automated rollback triggers unexpectedly, check per-segment confidence series and session-conflict counters in staging/production. Feature flag can be flipped off to revert to percentage-only ramps. Incident playbook reference: docs/operations/rollout_playbook.md#temporal-canaries
